mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) suggests accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to lower borrowing costs and increased liquidity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1%, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) and falling real estate sales (HOUST) indicates a demand-side shock, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending power diminishes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month AND HOUST decreases > 5%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of rising CPIAUCSL and falling HOUST on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4%) in a late-cycle expansion regime suggests tight labor markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies invest in productivity-enhancing technologies.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between low UNRATE and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in the specified regime.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising industrial production (INDPRO) and falling federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) suggests a supportive environment for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity picks up with accommodative monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% in 1 month AND FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of rising INDPRO and falling FEDFUNDS on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
